prompt_en: A complex photographic scene holds one coherent moment with a fictional adult woman in a theater prop repair room just after the final curtain. The supplied image guides her visible face and hair appearance: a short dark bob, airy divided bangs, soft oval face, large dark almond eyes, small nose and full lips. Across a scarred worktable, she looks toward the photographer with a neutral engaged expression while finishing an ordinary repair. Her plain buttoned cotton work shirt is neatly fastened, with sleeves pushed back from the wrists. Both forearms rest lightly on the tabletop; her right fingertips rest on a domed red enamel paperweight seated fully on the curling corner of a hand-painted scenery plan, while her left palm spreads its opposite edge flat. A previously rolled portion still arcs upward behind the flattened corner. Curtain folds and rolled scenery lean against the distant wall, placing this ordinary repair task after a public performance. A chest-height three-quarter view from the opposite side shows her face, both connected arms, the paper and weight together; her face and working hands lead the frame. One declared red object retains its red color: the saturated crimson enamel paperweight beneath her fingertips. The rest of the picture is achromatic, including skin, lips, eyes, hair, shirt, paper, curtains and wood, all equal-channel neutral grayscale. Dark image tones are lifted to visible gray, including the darkest hair roots and shelf recesses sitting distinctly at soft charcoal. Dark subject information remains readable as separate strands and shelf grain against that elevated tonal floor. Skin color transitions remain locally even through restrained local dodge-and-burn across her cheeks. Fine skin texture remains visible without facial-geometry alteration: fine pores and tiny natural variations stay crisp. Broad side window light shapes her face and table; smooth highlights and gently receding background preserve the eyes, cheeks and fingertips.
